Activate sustained research in `papers/master` in the smooth-poincare-4d checkout. Use GPT-6.2 Astra at ultra reasoning effort as lead. You have broad authority to try different proof routes, revisit earlier choices, consult primary literature, revise or create B decisions and E packets, and create bounded GPT-6.2 Sol helpers at ultra effort for derivations, counterexamples and independent proof checks. Continue through useful follow-on work without asking for routine approval.

Read `AGENTS.md`, the root README, the investigation, model and reference workflows, and this note at `papers/master/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md`. Read the master overview, plan, sole register, manuscript and initial review. Check current commits and working-tree revisions of the inputs you use. Follow the overview to the owning investigation and exact theorem or formalization receipt before relying on a result. Reconcile any later changes with the live register.

Start B02 and B03 in parallel. For B02, choose a construction available on an arbitrary smooth homotopy four-sphere and test whether it gives a positive Yamabe class with chiral energy strictly below $8\pi^2$. Check both positivity and the transition energy without assuming a standard smooth parametrization of the whole sphere. For B03, assume entry and choose one positive-class minimizing sequence of volume-one Yamabe representatives. Seek an actual marked cut separating two positive chiral masses, or an inexpensive same-type replacement of the volume-bearing marked balls together with an independent estimate on their complement. Use the quantitative targets above. A direct positive class of energy at most $4\pi^2$, or another direct recognition argument, can shorten the route at any stage.

Make each comparison on specified domains and smooth types. Track the physical metric and measures, the conformal or rescaled comparison metric, the boundary marking, both full sides, the cap signs and costs, and the order of limits. For a weak chart, choose the buffer length before passing to the source limit and test the first-order estimate in the chart where the splice is performed. If concentration persists, follow the missing chiral mass. Test a whole marked base, an admissible ALE component or another comparison justified on the selected sequence. Any use of almost Bach-flat compactness needs a source of small Bach error in the required norm at the minimizing energy. For a round restart at equal energy seek a termination argument. For an attained closed nonround minimizer seek rigidity or a strict same-type competitor. Record which cases remain reachable after each result.

Freeze each helper request in `papers/master/research-progress/handoffs/` with its ID, versioned inputs, mathematical target, finite scope, acceptance test, failure condition and distinct output. Keep shared files under lead ownership. Have an independent reader recompute the decisive step of a promising route. If a test fails, preserve the failed estimate and the class it covers, then choose the next route in light of that evidence. The first packets are starting points. You may change the mechanism, introduce a new intermediate result or use a shorter proof whenever the hypotheses support it.

Integrate assessed derivations and scoped failures into the master research record. Keep the register authoritative, provenance in the overview and forward decisions in the plan. Promote a verified result to the self-contained manuscript when it advances the principal proof. Rebuild the PDF after manuscript changes. At a substantial integrated milestone, report the strongest new implication, its hypotheses, the exact remaining obstruction and a concrete continuation.

I’ll check the master manuscript and its source revisions, then start the entry construction and the minimizing-sequence comparison in parallel. I’ll trace each estimate to the metric and marked domain on which it was proved.

The entry test has identified a limit of inserting a round bulb into an arbitrary metric. The bulb contributes zero Weyl energy, but the energy on the exterior survives. On the descent side, I found a way to use fixed-type minimization directly on a supplied chart. I’m checking whether it rules out hidden chiral energy there without a global Bach-error estimate.

The short-collar argument passed its independent check. Once a fixed annulus is spliced to an exact round product, that product can be lengthened on the original manifold to prove positivity of both caps. The source therefore needs first-order control only on the two short splices. I’m now checking what the same variational argument implies at the radius carrying half the chiral energy.

The scale comparison now gives a statement on the physical metrics themselves. If maximum curvature diverges, every ball of fixed radius in the maximum-curvature rescaling carries vanishing integrated curvature, uniformly over its center. I’ve also checked the bounded-curvature alternative, which leads to a smooth closed minimizer. The remaining concentration problem is locating the chiral mass at the larger scales.

**A positive-class minimizing sequence cannot carry a fixed amount of curvature energy at its maximum-curvature scale.** This is Corollary 8.2 of the rebuilt [master manuscript, p. 19](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/output/pdf/master/chiral_weyl_energy_and_smooth_poincare.pdf).

Assume a hypothetical nonstandard smooth homotopy four-sphere admits a positive Yamabe class with \(E_+<8\pi^2\). Choose volume-one Yamabe metrics \(g_i\) with \(E_+(g_i)\to I^+(M)\), and put \(K_i=\max_M|\mathrm{Rm}_{g_i}|\). If \(K_i\to\infty\), then for every fixed \(A>0\),
\[
\sup_{x\in M}\int_{B_{g_i}(x,A/\sqrt{K_i})}
          |\mathrm{Rm}_{g_i}|^2\,dV_{g_i}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently the least physical radius \(r_i\) carrying half the positive chiral energy satisfies \(r_i\sqrt{K_i}\to\infty\). If \(K_i\) stays bounded along a subsequence, the infimum is attained by a smooth closed minimizer on the original smooth type.

The decisive step was to replace the metric on a marked region while keeping the entire exterior fixed. Minimization then forces strong local convergence of both chiral energies and gives the Bach equation on the limit. This permits the use of end regularity there without assuming a small Bach error on the source sequence. A separate argument shows that two controlled **short** splices suffice for positive Yamabe caps on both full sides. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn936779925view0","turn370288660view2","turn773521343view3"]}}

**The next geometric test is at two chiral energy radii.** If a smaller ball carries a fixed fraction of the energy at radius \(o(r_i)\), its center gives two actual mass sets: the inner ball and the exterior of the median-radius ball. A low-curvature annulus lies between them. The missing step is a marked spherical chart on that annulus with the first-order control needed for the splice. If no such radii separate, every \(o(r_i)\)-ball carries a vanishing chiral fraction, and the comparison must account for energy distributed across the larger region.

Universal entry also remains open. Round insertion preserves the seed’s fixed sign and energy margins, and the tested fixed-area branched-cover smoothings force both chiral energies to diverge. A same-energy round restart and a closed nonround minimizer remain possible. I’ll verify the manuscript and its source revisions, then test what the two chiral radii imply about the geometry of an actual cut. In parallel I’ll examine a different entry construction and the alternatives in which the energy stays on a round restart or a closed minimizer.

The separated radii give two charged regions and a low-curvature annulus between them. I’ve found a way to construct the missing coordinates if the physical trace-free Ricci tensor satisfies a scaled \(L^p\) bound for some \(p>2\). I’m checking the compactness step and testing how much of that bound must hold on the annulus itself.

The Ricci-scale argument now has an independent check. It uses the topology of the source to rule out a nonflat Ricci-flat limit at a failing harmonic radius. On the diffuse branch, the repair calculation gives a different outcome: flattening a smooth disk with nonzero Weyl curvature increases its leading energy cost. I’m incorporating both results and checking a separate recognition test using height functions of an immersion into \(\mathbb R^5\).

Counting the index-two critical points of immersion heights gives a stronger result than counting all critical points together. The calculation points to direct smooth recognition from the induced metric at \(E_+\le 64\pi^2/9\), without a Yamabe-sign assumption. I’m having the handle argument and the equality case checked separately before promoting it.

The direct recognition proof passed both checks. It also narrows the surviving immersed case below \(8\pi^2\): more than three quarters of height directions have exactly two index-two critical points. I’ve added the proof to the manuscript and am checking the rebuilt PDF and the source revisions against the live register.

**The strongest result is direct smooth recognition at \(64\pi^2/9\) for hypersurface-induced conformal classes.** Let \(M\) be a smooth homotopy four-sphere. If one smooth immersion \(F:M\to\mathbb R^5\) induces a metric with
\[
E_+(F^*g_{\mathrm{Eucl}})\le \frac{64\pi^2}{9},
\]
then \(M\) is diffeomorphic to the standard \(S^4\). Equality is included, and there is no Yamabe-sign hypothesis. [Manuscript, Theorem 3.1](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/manuscript/immersion_entry.tex)

The proof counts index-two critical points of immersion heights. On a hypothetical nonstandard sphere, every Morse height needs at least two. Their average forces a lower bound on chiral energy where the shape operator has signature \((2,2)\). Codazzi and the Gauss equation exclude equality on that open set. The handle reduction and the equality argument received independent checks. [Handle check](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/reviews/E33_INDEX_TWO_HANDLES.md) · [Curvature check](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/reviews/E34_MIDDLE_WEYL_EQUALITY.md)

**The remaining geometric hypothesis is quantitative control of one immersion.** Every smooth homotopy four-sphere admits an immersion into \(\mathbb R^5\). Obtaining the energy bound on an arbitrary smooth type remains open. Even the weaker bound \(E_+<8\pi^2\) narrows the next step: on a nonstandard candidate, more than three quarters of height directions would have exactly two index-two critical points. One can therefore select an actual two-middle-handle decomposition and examine its attaching maps. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn133579609view2","turn274441922search0"]}}

On the **intrinsic minimizing-sequence route**, a whole harmonic marking of sufficiently small fixed distortion on the selected low-curvature shell now suffices for the separating cut. Constructing that marking around the two charged sets remains open. On the diffuse branch, a boundary-matched flattening of a regular disk cannot save a fixed fraction of its leading chiral energy. [Cut proof](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/manuscript/critical_annulus.tex) · [Diffuse repair calculation](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/notes/E17_DIFFUSE_REPAIR.md)

I’d pursue **four parallel investigations**. Two belong under a new hypersurface-immersion project, one already has a natural home in neck geometry, and one belongs directly under `papers/master`. The distinction is what each project must produce: a metric, a handle cancellation, a separating chart, or a lower-energy competitor.

**I’d launch 1, 2, and 3 first, and give 4 a fourth session if available.** Routes 1 and 2 can begin simultaneously. The construction group asks whether an arbitrary smooth type admits an immersion meeting the energy bound. The topology group can already work out what a subcritical immersion forces about its attaching maps. Route 3 is independent of hypersurface immersibility and has the clearest immediate payoff: one successful extraction closes the separated-mass case.

Route 4 is the natural **master sub-investigation** because its central object is the master’s fixed-smooth-type infimum. I’d keep flow-based selection with the existing Bach-flow investigation, which can contribute if it produces small Bach error *at that infimum*.

The master plan makes the coverage requirement explicit. Different routes may recognize different smooth types. To prove SPC4, their combined hypotheses must cover **every** hypothetical nonstandard homotopy four-sphere. On the variational route, it suffices to produce one suitable minimizing sequence for each type reached by positive entry. On the immersion route, the construction and recognition arguments must apply to the **same immersion and its actual attaching maps**.

The [four launch prompts](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/continuation-notes/PARALLEL_PROGRAM_20261125.md) are ready for independent sessions. Each branch has a sole progress register, and exploratory work stays with its owner until a checked result advances the master proof.
